description: Average Cost of Supply minus Average Revenue Realised, per unit of electricity sold. Positive = the utility loses money on every unit it sells (closed by tariff hike, loss reduction, or state subsidy). Zero is the UDAY/RDSS policy goal.
Final energy consumed in the agriculture sector via electricity, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Final energy consumed in the agriculture sector via gas, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Final energy consumed in the agriculture sector via oil, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Count of artificial-insemination EVENTS performed under NAIP IV (district SoT; auto-rolled to state per ADR-0043). Repeat inseminations on the same animal are counted multiple times.
Total nameplate generating capacity in megawatts, summed across all fuels, for India. Snapshot end-of-month from the CEA Monthly Executive Summary.

Combined technical (transmission + distribution heat / ageing losses) and commercial (theft + uncollected billing) losses as % of energy input to the distribution system. Headline discom-health metric: lower is better.
Share of energy actually billed to a consumer, out of total energy input to the distribution system. 100% = every kWh that enters the grid was billed.

Modelled maximum bio-energy capacity (MW) a state could build, summed across the two physically-additive streams the assessment publishes: agricultural / forestry biomass and bagasse-based cogeneration at sugar mills. This is buildable potential driven by a state's crop residue and sugar industry, NOT installed capacity and NOT a policy achievement.

Biomass / bio-power PLF (publisher label: 'bio-power'). Feedstock-supply-bounded; agricultural-residue-rich states (Punjab, Haryana, UP, Tamil Nadu) show higher PLFs only when supply chains are functional.
Biomass / bio-power procurement share. Tied to agri-residue feedstock availability; meaningful in Punjab, Haryana, UP, Tamil Nadu when supply chains function.
Number of buffaloes tagged with Pashu Aadhaar (NDLM) in each district. Tagged count, NOT actual buffaloes population.
Count of calves born per district from NAIP IV inseminations during FY 2024-25. Publisher reports sex split (male/female); this lift collapses sex via SUM.
Absolute number of votes a candidate received in a single AC contest.
Full field size: kept candidates plus those collapsed into the 'others' tail by the top-N cutoff.
Total number of candidates contesting a Parliament parliamentary constituency.

Same as the geographical-location capacity, but each state credited its share of joint-sector and central-sector plants per regional allocation formulas. Use this when comparing 'rights to electricity' rather than 'physical assets sited here'.
Auto-minted stub for indicator state-installed-capacity-allocated-mw.

Total installed capacity physically located in the state, summed across all fuels. 'Geographical' means every plant counts toward the state where it sits, regardless of who owns it or where the power is dispatched.

Total installed capacity allocated to each state at the end of the most recent month, from the CEA Monthly Executive Summary IC sheet. Snapshot view; complements the multi-FY ICED geographical and allocated series.

Installed capacity (MW) of captive power plants - generation that industry builds and runs behind the meter for its own use, summed across all industry categories in a state. A high captive total often signals industry routing around an unreliable or expensive public grid by self-generating, rather than a policy achievement. Self-reported by industry to the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) and widely understood to be under-reported, so read the totals as a lower bound, not a precise census. The all-India aggregate row and the source's combined 'Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh' label (which cannot be split across the two post-2019 entities) are not included.

Electricity generated (GWh) by captive power plants - the energy industry produces behind the meter for its own use, summed across all industry categories in a state. High captive generation often signals industry self-supplying because the public grid is unreliable or costly. The CEA reports this in Million Units (MU); 1 MU equals 1 GWh exactly, so the values are unchanged under the GWh label. Self-reported by industry to the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) and widely understood to be under-reported, so read the totals as a lower bound, not a precise census. The all-India aggregate row and the source's combined 'Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh' label (which cannot be split across the two post-2019 entities) are not included.
Number of cattle tagged with Pashu Aadhaar (NDLM) in each district. Tagged count, NOT actual cattle population.
Final energy consumed in the cgd and others sector via gas, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Coal-fired generation. ~70% of all-India electricity by GWh (PLF gap between capacity share and generation share).
Coal share of total primary energy supply. The dominant TPES bucket since FY05 (~55% in recent years).

Per-state domestic coal consumption in million tonnes per fiscal year, summed across all coal grades (raw + washed + middlings + lignite). High values typically indicate hosting large thermal generation fleets (Maharashtra, UP, MP, Chhattisgarh) or heavy industry (steel, cement).

Share (%) of a state's OPERATING coal-power capacity fitted with FGD (flue-gas desulphurisation / SO2 scrubbers) - an air-quality enforcement metric tracking how much of the running coal fleet meets the SO2-emission norm. Each plant is geocoded to its state by coordinates (point-in-polygon against the LGD state boundaries); the numerator counts operating units whose FGD is installed, the denominator all operating coal units. A geocode-derived (major-processing) statistic.

State-grain BENEFICIARY share of coal-fired capacity (ISGS/PSU contractual allocation). A Mundra plant sited in Gujarat is allocated to multiple states by quota. Distinct measure from geographical siting.
Coal-fired thermal capacity retired each fiscal year (flow, not stock). Distinct measure from installed coal capacity.
Coal-fired plant load factor: how hard the state's coal fleet is being run. 60%+ = healthy despatch, 40% = structural underuse (stranded assets), regulator-set floor varies.

Share of state's procured electricity that came from coal plants. India-wide ~70% historically; declining as RE rises. Coal-importing states (Karnataka, Maharashtra, Punjab) typically run above the average.
Share of billed revenue actually collected from consumers, by state. 100% = every rupee billed was paid.
Final energy consumed in the commercial sector via electricity, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Final energy consumed in the commercial sector via oil, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Number of distinct ACs in the state where this party fielded a candidate.
High-speed diesel: the dominant refined petroleum product. Tracks transport activity (heavy vehicles, buses, trucks) and agricultural pump-set use; the largest single fuel by volume in every state.
Diesel-genset procurement share. Typically <1% across most states; an emergency-backup category, not a baseload source.

Compute-on-read parent: the three citizen-readable sub-indicators of distribution-side efficiency â€” billing efficiency, collection efficiency, and T&D loss. The first two decompose the COMMERCIAL half of AT&C losses; the third is the TECHNICAL half.
Number of donkeys tagged with Pashu Aadhaar (NDLM) in each district. Tagged count, NOT actual donkeys population.
1 / sum(vote_share_squared). Higher = more fragmented contest.
Laakso-Taagepera effective number of candidates (inverse Herfindahl of vote shares) in a Parliament parliamentary constituency.
1 / sum(seat_share_squared) across parties. Higher = more fragmented legislature.
Number of voters on the electoral roll for this AC as of election day.
Total enrolled electors in a single Parliament parliamentary constituency contest.

Share of newly-registered vehicles that are electric, in percent - the EV-transition signal. For each state and year, the count of newly-registered electric vehicles (all vehicle categories) divided by the count of ALL newly-registered vehicles. This is a share of NEW registrations in the year, NOT the share of vehicles on the road; the on-road stock turns over slowly, so the stock share lags this flow share by years.
Count of unique farmers in each district reached by NAIP IV inseminations during FY 2024-25.

India's final energy consumption in million tonnes of oil equivalent (mtoe) - the energy actually delivered to and used by end-use demand sectors, after conversion losses. Reported as a sector x fuel matrix: eight demand sectors (agriculture, industry, transport, residential, commercial, the city-gas-distribution 'CGD and others' bucket, the non-energy feedstock use, and a residual 'other') against four delivered carriers (coal, oil, gas, electricity). Electricity appears here as a DELIVERED carrier (final consumption counts the electricity a sector uses, not the coal/gas/hydro that generated it - that lives in primary supply). The matrix is sparse - not every sector uses every fuel. National series only (no per-state split is published).
Number of ACs where the party's candidate received less than 1/6 of valid votes (Section 158, Representation of the People Act).
Gas-fired generation. Capacity-rich, generation-poor due to fuel-supply constraints.

State-grain BENEFICIARY share of gas-fired capacity (ISGS/PSU contractual allocation). A Hazira plant sited in Gujarat may be allocated to multiple states by quota. Distinct measure from geographical siting.
Gas/oil/diesel-fired thermal capacity retired each fiscal year (flow, not stock). Distinct measure from installed gas capacity.
Gas-fired plant load factor (publisher bucket 'oil-gas' = natural gas + diesel + furnace oil). Persistently low in India (often <25%) due to gas allocation shortages -- not a despatch failure.
Gas-fired procurement share (publisher 'oil-gas' bucket: natural gas + furnace oil). Often <5% due to gas-allocation shortages limiting plant availability.
Number of goats tagged with Pashu Aadhaar (NDLM) in each district. Tagged count, NOT actual goats population.
Number of horses tagged with Pashu Aadhaar (NDLM) in each district. Tagged count, NOT actual horses population.
Bundled-hybrid PPA procurement share (wind + solar + storage sold as one contract). A procurement-channel category, not a single fuel. Emerging post-2022 as MNRE hybrid policy ramped.
Hydroelectric generation. Seasonal (monsoon-dependent) and falling as a share over time.
Large hydro share of TPES (>=25 MW). Inter-annual swings track monsoon variability; structurally flat as no major new dams have been commissioned recently.

State-grain BENEFICIARY share of hydro capacity (ISGS/PSU contractual allocation). A large hydro station sited in one hill state may be allocated to multiple consumer states by quota. Distinct measure from geographical siting.
Final energy consumed in the industry sector via coal, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Final energy consumed in the industry sector via electricity, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Final energy consumed in the industry sector via gas, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Final energy consumed in the industry sector via oil, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Superior kerosene oil: household lighting + cooking fuel from the legacy PDS era. Declines steeply post-PMUY as LPG replaces it; near-zero in many states by FY23.
Owners in the landless / marginal bracket (<1 Ha) registered on Bharat Pashudhan. Registered count, NOT all owning households.
Owners in the large-holding bracket (>=10 Ha) registered on Bharat Pashudhan. Registered count, NOT all owning households.
Large-hydro plant load factor (capacity > 25 MW). Inherently seasonal; monsoon-dependent states show high inter-year variation that is RESOURCE-driven, not fleet-performance-driven.
Large-hydro (>25 MW) procurement share. Higher in hill states (HP, UK, Sikkim) and seasonally variable across monsoon vs winter.
Count of livestock owners completed Bharat Pashudhan registration. Registered count, NOT all owning households.

Liquefied petroleum gas: household cooking-fuel after the PMUY (Ujjwala) scheme. Tracks household-coverage policy more than wealth -- rural states with successful PMUY rollout show high per-capita LPG consumption.
floor(total_acs / 2) + 1. Constant per state per delimitation cycle.
Vote-margin between winner and runner-up as a percentage of total votes polled.
Winner's votes minus runner-up's votes.
Vote margin between the winner and the runner-up in a Parliament parliamentary constituency.
Winner-minus-runner-up margin as a percentage of total votes polled in a Parliament parliamentary constituency.
Owners in the medium bracket (4.0-9.99 Ha) registered on Bharat Pashudhan. Registered count, NOT all owning households.
Number of mithun tagged with Pashu Aadhaar (NDLM) in each district. Tagged count, NOT actual mithun population.
Number of mules tagged with Pashu Aadhaar (NDLM) in each district. Tagged count, NOT actual mules population.
Light hydrocarbon feedstock for petrochemicals + occasional power-plant fuel. Concentrated in petrochemical-cluster states (Gujarat, Maharashtra). Volatile year-on-year.
Natural-gas share of TPES (domestic + LNG imports). The fastest-growing fossil bucket; tracks LNG-terminal commissioning and pipeline expansion.
Final energy consumed in the non energy sector via gas, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Final energy consumed in the non energy sector via oil, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Share of the state's non-solar (wind + biomass + small-hydro) RPO target actually met. The 'other-renewables' segment of the obligation, regulated separately from the solar segment.
Owners who did not declare a land-holding bracket while registering on Bharat Pashudhan. Preserved verbatim, not imputed.
NOTA votes as a percentage of votes polled. Null pre-2013.
NOTA votes as a percentage of total votes polled in a Parliament parliamentary constituency. Null before 2013.
Absolute number of NOTA (None of the Above) votes. Null pre-2013.
None-of-the-above votes cast in a Parliament parliamentary constituency. Null before NOTA was introduced (2013).
Nuclear generation. Small share but rising as new units commission.
Nuclear share of TPES. Small fleet (~7 GW operational); structurally flat with episodic step changes when a new reactor commissions.

State-grain BENEFICIARY share of nuclear capacity (NPCIL central-sector PPA allocation). A reactor sited in one state is allocated to multiple consumer states by quota. Distinct measure from geographical siting.
Nuclear plant load factor. Only present in states hosting reactors (TN/Karnataka/Rajasthan/Gujarat/Maharashtra/UP); rest = no data. Targets 80%+ when fuel-supply and grid-offtake align.
Nuclear procurement share. Allocated centrally from NPCIL plants; states near reactors (TN, KA, MH, RJ, GJ, UP) have higher shares.
Crude-oil + petroleum-products share of TPES. The second-largest bucket; tracks transport-fleet activity and refinery throughput.

Per-state annual consumption of refined petroleum products in kilotonnes, broken down by 7 products (diesel-HSD, petrol, LPG, kerosene, naphtha, petroleum-coke, others). Diesel dominates everywhere; LPG tracks PMUY rollout; petroleum-coke tracks industrial heat use.
Final energy consumed in the other sector via electricity, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Final energy consumed in the other sector via oil, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Other-renewables procurement share (publisher 'other-res' bucket): waste-to-energy and small uncategorised RE. Typically <1-2% across most states.
Publisher catch-all for products outside the 6 named buckets (fuel oil, ATF, lubricants, bitumen, etc.). Preserved verbatim, never imputed into a named bucket.
Aggregate % vote-share for the collapsed tail. Absent when no tail exists.
Aggregated 'others' votes as a percentage of total votes polled in a Parliament parliamentary constituency.
Sum of votes for candidates below the top-N cutoff. Absent when no tail exists.
Votes for all candidates outside the top finishers, aggregated, in a Parliament parliamentary constituency.
Sum of all votes received by the party's candidates across the state.
Count of animals issued a 12-digit Pashu Aadhaar tag in each district. Tagged count, NOT actual population.

Highest single-instant electricity demand observed in the state during the fiscal year (MW). 'Peak' is system-wide simultaneous demand recorded by the State Load Despatch Centre â€” typically a summer afternoon (north / west) or winter evening (Punjab, Delhi).

Maximum instantaneous power actually supplied in the state during the fiscal year (MW). The pair (peak_demand, peak_supplied) tells the load-shedding story: supplied < demand in any year means the grid dropped load to keep frequency stable.

Annual per-capita electricity availability (kWh / person / year), by state and Union Territory, fiscal year. The most citizen-relevant single number for 'how much power do people in this state actually get to use' â€” captures both supply expansion and transmission losses.
Auto-minted stub for indicator per-capita-electricity-availability-kwh.

Electricity consumption per person per year, in kilowatt-hours. Proxy for BOTH energy access (electrified homes) AND industrial intensity (heavy-industry load) â€” read alongside per-capita income to disambiguate.
Auto-minted stub for indicator per-capita-electricity-consumption-kwh.
Motor spirit (gasoline): cars, two-wheelers, light vehicles. A proxy for urban-personal-mobility intensity; rises with vehicle ownership and middle-class growth.
Refinery by-product used as cheap industrial fuel (cement, glass, steel). Heavily regulated for air-quality reasons in NCR and some industrial states. Tracks heavy-industry heat use.
Number of pigs tagged with Pashu Aadhaar (NDLM) in each district. Tagged count, NOT actual pigs population.

Share of nameplate capacity actually delivered as energy over a fiscal year. Per state, per fuel source. Coal PLFs near 60% indicate healthy merit-order despatch; near 40% indicates structural underuse.
Annual energy actually supplied to the state (MU = million units = GWh), fiscal year. The supply-side companion to Requirement (T141). Requirement âˆ’ Availability = the energy-not-supplied deficit.

Share of total electricity purchased by a state's distribution utilities, broken down by generation source. The procurement mix (where DISCOMs buy from), not the generation mix (what plants produce). Values sum to ~100% per (state, FY).

Annual energy requirement assessed by the state (MU = million units = GWh), fiscal year â€” the demand-side counterpart to availability. Requirement minus availability gives the 'energy not supplied' deficit.
Count of pregnancy-diagnosis EVENTS performed under NAIP IV (district SoT; auto-rolled to state per ADR-0043). A single dam may be diagnosed multiple times in the same year.

India's Total Primary Energy Supply (TPES) in million tonnes of oil equivalent (mtoe), broken out by the six primary sources the national energy balance recognises (coal, oil, gas, hydro, nuclear, renewables). 'Primary' means energy as it enters the economy before conversion to electricity or fuels - so coal here is the coal burned across all uses, NOT just power-sector coal, and renewables / hydro / nuclear are counted as the primary energy they supply. The six sources sum to TPES; this is a national series only (no per-state split is published).
Ordinal rank by votes polled (1 = winner).
Wind, solar and biomass generation. ~10% all-India share by FY26; growing fast.

Cumulative grid-connected renewable installed capacity in MW, end-March snapshot per year. Combined wind + solar + small-hydro + biomass + waste-to-energy (publisher emits no per-source split). Rajasthan, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Maharashtra dominate.
State-grain BENEFICIARY share of renewable capacity (ISGS/PSU contractual allocation; a plant sited in one state is allocated to multiple consumer states). Distinct measure from geographical siting.
Aggregate renewable share of TPES (solar + wind + biomass + small-hydro + waste-to-energy). The fastest-growing bucket; publisher emits as a single aggregate, not broken into RE sub-fuels.
Final energy consumed in the residential sector via electricity, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Final energy consumed in the residential sector via oil, in mtoe per fiscal year.

Cumulative installed rooftop solar PV capacity in megawatts. Building-mounted (residential + commercial + industrial + public) only; utility-scale solar is separate and lives under installed-capacity-snapshot-mw (renewable facet).

Compute-on-read parent: the three citizen-readable segments of state RPO compliance â€” solar, non-solar, and combined-target. Each measures share of the regulatory RPO target met, expressed as compliance Ã· target Ã— 100.
NITI Aayog SDG India Index composite score (0-100): a state/UT's distance to the 2030 SDG targets. A policy-dashboard index, not a direct outcome measure.
Number of ACs the party won in this state election.
Owners in the semi-medium bracket (2.0-3.99 Ha) registered on Bharat Pashudhan. Registered count, NOT all owning households.
Number of sheep tagged with Pashu Aadhaar (NDLM) in each district. Tagged count, NOT actual sheep population.
Owners in the small-holding bracket (1.0-1.99 Ha) registered on Bharat Pashudhan. Registered count, NOT all owning households.
Small-hydro plant load factor (capacity <= 25 MW). Run-of-river dominated; seasonal-flow-bounded. Distinct from large-hydro for despatch and resource-availability reasons.
Small-hydro (<=25 MW) procurement share. Distinct from large hydro; counts under most state RPO obligations.

Modelled maximum solar PV capacity (MW) a state could build, estimated by the National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE) from the headline scenario of 3% of the state's wasteland area at current module efficiency. This is buildable potential driven by geography (desert / arid land / irradiation), NOT installed capacity and NOT a policy achievement - a large potential is an endowment, not a ranking of effort.

Solar PLF (utility + rooftop combined). Resource-bounded: even perfect operation cannot exceed ~22-25% in India (function of sunlight hours). A 20% solar PLF is GOOD; do NOT compare to a 60% coal target.
Solar procurement share (utility + rooftop). Rajasthan, Gujarat, Karnataka lead with double-digit shares; smaller eastern states still in single digits.
Share of the state's solar-specific RPO target actually met. 100% = solar-RPO target exactly met; values above 100% indicate over-compliance on solar procurement.
Sum of enrolled electors across all ACs in the state.

Total electricity actually billed to end-consumers (domestic + commercial + industrial + agricultural + public-lighting) in the state, in million units (MU). The gap between Generation and Sales is the absolute AT&C loss.
Per-state actual electricity generated, summed across all fuels. The delivered counterpart to installed capacity â€” capacity is potential, generation is what plants actually produced.
Sum of NOTA votes across state as % of votes polled. Null pre-2013.
State-level votes polled as % of state-level enrolled electors.
Sum of votes polled across all ACs in the state.
Seats won as a percentage of seats contested by the party.

Transmission substation capacity commissioned per year, by voltage class; national. The summed nameplate capacity (MVA) of transmission substations brought into service each fiscal year, grouped by their governing (highest) voltage tier. An indicator of grid build-out - how much high-voltage switching/transformation capacity the country adds each year. The source carries NO state attribution, so this is a national-only series; it is NOT installed generation capacity and NOT a per-state ranking.
Transmission and Distribution loss as % of energy input â€” the TECHNICAL half of AT&C losses (heat / ageing / unmetered consumption on the wires).

National total of thermal generating capacity retired each fiscal year, broken down by fuel (coal vs gas). A key signal in the energy-transition story: rising coal retirements means the fleet is being replaced, not just expanded.
Combined-target RPO compliance â€” share of the state's overall (solar + non-solar combined) RPO target met. NOT the sum of solar + non-solar â€” the combined target is its own regulatory ratio.

Procurement via power exchanges (IEX / PXIL) + unscheduled interchange (UI). Source-agnostic at procurement time. Higher trading share = state buys spot to meet demand fluctuations, not necessarily a stress signal.
Final energy consumed in the transport sector via electricity, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Final energy consumed in the transport sector via oil, in mtoe per fiscal year.
Votes polled as a percentage of total enrolled electors.
Votes polled as a percentage of total enrolled electors in a Parliament parliamentary constituency.

Power generation capacity in active construction (post-financial-close, pre-commissioning), by expected commission calendar-year. Distinct from commissioned installed capacity and from retired capacity; this measures FUTURE additions not yet generating.
A single candidate's votes as a percentage of total votes polled in their AC (including NOTA).
A party's votes summed across all its candidates as a percentage of total votes polled in the state.
Sum of all candidate votes plus NOTA in this AC contest.
Sum of all candidate votes plus NOTA in this Parliament parliamentary constituency contest.

Modelled maximum wind capacity (MW) a state could build, estimated by the National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE) at 150 metres above ground level (the current headline hub height). This is buildable potential driven by geography (wind corridors, coastline, terrain), NOT installed capacity and NOT a policy achievement - a few states with strong wind corridors dominate the national total.

Wind PLF. Resource-bounded by site quality (Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Karnataka coastal/desert zones are wind-rich). A 25% wind PLF in Tamil Nadu is excellent; same number in a low-wind state could be aspirational siting.
Wind procurement share. Resource-bounded; Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Rajasthan dominate as both producers AND consumers (sold within state and via inter-state PPAs).
entity_id of the candidate who received the most votes. Stored in value_text.
entity_id of the candidate who received the most votes in a Parliament parliamentary constituency. Stored in value_text.
party_id of the winning candidate in a single Assembly Constituency contest (seat-level outcome; parties.IN.IND for independents).
party_id of the winning candidate in a single Parliament parliamentary constituency contest (seat-level outcome; parties.IN.IND for independents).
party_id with the most seats statewide (state-aggregate majority outcome; null on a hung house).
Seats held by the state's winning party.
Number of yaks tagged with Pashu Aadhaar (NDLM) in each district. Tagged count, NOT actual yaks population.
